title: 1. The Mystery of the Train Ticket (Hook)
content: Have you ever held a real train ticket? It's not just a piece of paper; it's a secret code with your journey's details! Imagine you are a detective trying to find where Omana is going.

title: 2. Be a Detective (Socratic Thinking)
content: If you found a train ticket on the floor, what clues would you look for to know where the person is going? Would it have their name, or their destination?

content.title: Parts of a Train Ticket
content.description: A close-up of a train ticket highlighting the PNR, Train Number, and Fare.

title: 4. Decoding the Ticket (Reveal)
content: A train ticket is a document that gives you permission to travel. It contains important details like the Train Number, Date of Journey, Seat Number, and the Fare (cost of the ticket).

description: The money you pay to travel by bus, train, taxi, etc.
Passenger Name Record. A unique number given to every ticket booked on a train.

question: Which of these details is usually NOT found on a train ticket?

content: Bring a real or printed train ticket to the class and let students find the PNR and Fare in groups.

title: 6. Why buy a ticket? (Reflection)
content: Think about why we need a ticket. What would happen if everyone travelled without buying a ticket? The railways would not have money to run the trains!

title: 7. Everywhere you go (Connection)
content: Just like train tickets, we also need tickets for buses, airplanes, and even the ferry that Omana took in Kerala! A ticket is your promise that you have paid for the journey.

title: 8. Ticket Explorer (Mastery)
content: Ask your parents to show you an old travel ticket (bus, train, or flight). Make a list of 5 things you can read on it!

title: 1. The Floating Bus (Hook)
content: Imagine a bus that floats on water! In Kerala, where there is water everywhere, how do people go to school, the market, or their grandmother's house?

title: 2. Crossing the River (Socratic Thinking)
content: If you had to cross a wide river and there was no bridge, what kind of vehicle would you use? How many people could it carry?

content.title: A Ferry in Kerala
content.description: A boat moving across the water carrying people and bicycles.

title: 4. Meet the Ferry! (Reveal)
content: Omana and her family took a Ferry to reach her grandmother's house. A ferry is a special boat used to carry passengers, bicycles, and sometimes even cars across water bodies.

description: A boat or ship used to carry people and goods across a river or a narrow body of water.
A part of a river where the water does not flow away, often forming a network of lakes and canals, very famous in Kerala.

question: What is a ferry used for?
options: To dig holes in the ground

content: Students often confuse a Ferry with a Ship. Remember: Ships travel on oceans for many days, but ferries usually travel across rivers or lakes for short journeys.

title: 6. Life on Water (Reflection)
content: Why do you think Kerala has so many ferries? In places where land is separated by many rivers and canals, boats are the easiest way to travel!

title: 7. Waterways of the World (Connection)
content: Kerala's backwaters are famous around the world. Just like roads connect cities on land, waterways connect villages in Kerala, and ferries are the buses of these waterways!

title: 8. Draw a Ferry (Mastery)
content: Draw a picture of a ferry carrying people and a few bicycles across a beautiful river in Kerala. Color it brightly!
